answers.text: Give back three lines every time - drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted - same order, same labels. If damage isn't mentioned, write 'none noted' instead of skipping the line.
List each call needing follow-up as its own line with time, customer, topic and outcome, and count those lines for the total.
The finish time doesn't work - 8am plus roughly six hours lands early afternoon the same day, the 22nd, not the 23rd as the note says.
96 to 118 is nearer 23% than the 20% the note gives.
Output 2 - it shows the 940 and 827 behind the 88%. Output 1 could still be right, it's just not possible to check without rerunning it.
Email 2, since it has the real volume numbers to back the ask. Email 1's claim isn't checkable as it stands, though it might turn out to be fair once the numbers are pulled.
The rates and retainer cap are sensitive, so I'd leave those out, and the non-disclosure clause makes me want to be careful with the rest too.
Before the summary goes out at month-end, I check the reconciled totals against the warehouse count, which would catch a wrong figure, not just a typo.

Step 4 needs the gate most since it submits automatically - I'd flag anything where the match to the PO is outside a small tolerance. Step 1 matters too, since a bad read there carries through everything after it.
